task.description: WF-03 Step 2b (hard gate) for ISS-0428: independently verify CODE-DESIGNER's design (lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md) actually closes the vacuous-ISS-0069-gate hazard, by running real experiments (inject a real unused-optional-default warning, run scripts/test_parallel.sh, confirm where it does/does not appear) rather than reasoning from the document alone -- plus judge the wholesale-switch reversal, failure-mode parity, the two serial subprocess runs, the ISS-0423 boundary, and confirm no implementation code is present.

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS, with one MAJOR and one MINOR finding -- no vacuous-pass path found, no implementation code present, every acceptance-criterion-shaped concern in ISS-0428 has a corresponding design element with no TBD/deferral language beyond explicitly-flagged, appropriately-scoped open questions (section 8).

=== THE CENTRAL EXPERIMENT (item 1 of dispatch) ===

Injected a real ISS-0069-shaped warning: test/support/iss0428_probe_helper.ex, a `defp probe_fn(a, unused_optional \\ :never_used)` where every call site passes the arg explicitly -- the exact shape docs/anti-patterns.md's 'A test helper's default argument goes dead...' entry documents (3 prior real occurrences: REQ-178/187/191). Confirmed the warning fires under plain `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --force`: quoted output `warning: default values for the optional arguments in the private function probe_fn/2 are never used`.

Ran `TEST_PARALLEL_N=2 bash scripts/test_parallel.sh test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs test/support/tenant_template_test.exs` (scoped to two small test files to fit the tool's execution budget -- N=2 matches CI's real parallelism, the design's own load-bearing case). Real output:
  - Aggregated stdout (scratch/probe_stdout.log, since deleted): `partition 1: 4 tests, 2 properties, 0 failures, exit 0` / `partition 2: 6 tests, 0 properties, 0 failures, exit 0` / `combined: 10 tests, 2 properties, 0 failures (12/12 passed)` -- i.e. the runner's own summary output never states 'warning' or the target substring in its per-partition/combined count lines, confirming §1.1's core premise that aggregate COUNT lines carry no diagnostic text.
  - BOTH partition-1.log and partition-2.log (grep -l confirmed both matched) contained the full warning text, including file/line attribution (`test/support/iss0428_probe_helper.ex:6:8`). The design's actual per-partition-log-substring-check mechanism (§1.2 steps 3-5) DOES catch the injected warning. This is the proof the dispatch demanded, and it holds.
  - Reverted the probe file, re-ran plain `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --force`, confirmed grep for the substring returns no match (clean).

=== FINDING 1 (MAJOR, not BLOCKER -- see reasoning) ===
file: lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md, section 1.1 (lines ~51-72)
summary: The design's own stated rationale for why re-pointing is necessary is factually imprecise -- it claims scripts/test_parallel.sh 'prints only aggregated pass/fail counts to stdout -- never the constituent partitions' raw text' and that pointing the check at that aggregate stdout 'finds nothing, forever.' This is not fully true: the script's Step 1 (`MIX_ENV=test mix compile`, scripts/test_parallel.sh:99) runs UNREDIRECTED, before any partition launches, so its own compiler-warning output (including an ISS-0069-shaped warning in test/support/) flows straight into the wrapper subprocess's own top-level stdout -- the same stream `stream_and_capture/2` would capture as 'the runner's own captured stdout' whether or not this design's re-pointing ships. Verified directly: my probe's warning appeared once in the aggregate stdout (scratch/probe_stdout.log line 3, immediately after 'pre-compiling MIX_ENV=test'), not zero times as §1.1 states.
failure_scenario: A future reader (implementer or reviewer) who trusts §1.1's literal claim and later needs to reason about why the substring check can't just grep the wrapper's own captured stdout (e.g. during a maintenance change, or when 3.1's error-handling code is touched) will reason from a false premise: 'the aggregate stream never carries the warning' is not true for compile-time warnings specifically, only for count-summary-line text. In THIS design's actual specified mechanism this causes no live defect (the algorithm never relies on the aggregate stdout being warning-free -- it only reads partition logs, per §1.2 step 4-5), so it is not a vacuous-pass hole. But it is exactly the kind of imprecise premise `docs/anti-patterns.md`'s 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' warns against, and it weakens the document's own stated justification for the re-pointing work in the eyes of the next reader who does not independently re-verify it (which is the entire point of a validator gate existing).
severity_rationale: Not a BLOCKER because I traced the actual algorithm (§1.2 steps 1-6) and confirmed by experiment it does not depend on the aggregate stdout being substring-free -- it is unambiguously specified to read only partition-*.log files, and I proved those logs DO reliably carry the warning (via Mix's own compile-manifest re-emission on each partition's own `mix test --partitions N` invocation against its hardlink-seeded `_build/test-partition-<i>` tree -- an already-documented project behavior, see mix.exs:88-90's own note about warnings re-emitted from the compile manifest even when nothing needs recompiling). MAJOR because a design document whose central risk section states a load-bearing empirical claim incorrectly is a real defect in a document whose entire purpose is to be trusted without re-derivation by ELIXIR-DEV -- route back to CODE-DESIGNER to correct §1.1's wording to state precisely what is true (aggregate stdout DOES echo compile-time warnings from the shared pre-compile step, but that is incidental/unreliable -- e.g. a warning in a file only reached via a partition-specific compile path, or one whose manifest entry is not re-emitted, would NOT appear there, which is the actually-correct reason per-partition-log-checking is still required) rather than the currently-stated absolute claim.

=== FINDING 2 (MINOR) ===
file: lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md, section 1.2, steps 2 vs 5
summary: Ordering between the 'partition-logs-in-<dir> line absent' error path (step 2) and the 'wrapper nonzero exit' error path (step 5) is not made explicit for the case where they co-occur -- which I confirmed is a real, non-hypothetical case, not merely possible in principle: a `mix compile` failure inside scripts/test_parallel.sh's Step 1 (before any partition launches) causes the script to exit nonzero (verified: exit 1) WITHOUT ever printing the 'partition logs in <dir>' line (verified: grep -c on captured stdout = 0). Both step 2's and step 5's failure conditions are true simultaneously in this case, and the design does not state which `Mix.raise` message a reader should expect, or whether `run_main_suite/0` must check exit code before or after attempting log-dir discovery.
failure_scenario: Not a correctness defect -- I confirmed both orderings converge on a hard failure (Mix.raise), never a silent pass, so this cannot produce a vacuous-pass hole. It is purely an implementability-ambiguity: ELIXIR-DEV could reasonably write the exit-code check first (natural reading of §1.2's step 5 test-and-substring-check framing, which most closely maps to today's `run/1` shape) or the log-discovery-first (natural reading of the numbered 1-6 list order as sequential). Either produces a correct, safe outcome, but TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER writing a regression test against 'the exact Mix.raise message for a compile-failure-during-parallel-run' would get a different expected string depending on which order ships, with no spec to check against.
severity_rationale: MINOR, not a gate-failing ambiguity per the role file's 'FAIL immediately on any single failed check' standard, because this is not an ambiguity in WHAT must happen (hard fail, always) -- only in the literal wording of the raised message, which is not itself an acceptance-criterion-bearing detail. Recording it so CODE-DESIGNER can add one sentence (e.g. 'check the wrapper's own exit code first; only attempt log-dir discovery if exit was 0 or the failure reason itself needs the logs') rather than leaving it to ELIXIR-DEV's implicit judgement call, consistent with the role file's 'don't approve a design because ELIXIR-DEV could probably figure out the gaps' standard -- flagging it rather than treating it as approved-by-omission.

=== OTHER DISPATCH ITEMS ===

Item 1 remaining sub-questions: (a) stability of the 'test_parallel: partition logs in <dir>' line -- read scripts/test_parallel.sh in full: printed unconditionally at line 215, only reachable after Step 1 (compile) and Step 1.5 (pool clamp) both succeed; a compile failure (verified above) or an early Step-0 N-derivation failure (no bash-parseable N) both exit before line 215, so the line is genuinely conditional on reaching Step 2 -- exactly the case the design's step 2 error-shape text covers, not a gap. (b) zero-partition-logs case: design states hard failure unambiguously (quoted above, §1.2 step 3's own italicized 'Error shape'); did not additionally reproduce this by fabricating a directory (would require editing scripts/test_parallel.sh, out of scope for this design and this gate), but the specified behavior is unambiguous text, satisfying the design-completeness bar this gate checks. (c) tmp_dir deletion: confirmed by grep -- no `rm -rf "$tmp_dir"` anywhere in scripts/test_parallel.sh; CI could still clean a /tmp path mid-job in principle but that is a pre-existing risk of the unmodified script, not introduced by this design, and §4.2 step 5 already argues CI's job-log retention (not the raw tmp dir) is the design's actual answer for CI.

Item 2 (wholesale switch): judged sound. §0's N=2 measurement (774s, 3214/3214 clean, no too_many_connections) is ORCH's own independently-run, quoted figure (step-00 handoff), not the design's own unverified claim -- re-read that handoff and confirmed the figures match what §0 cites. The reversal of ISS-0428's own 'selectable, CI unchanged' hedge is argued (not merely asserted) on the specific ground that the hedge's own stated justification (CI gains unproven, N=2 might hit connection exhaustion) is now empirically closed by that same measurement -- a fair argument. §3.1's bash-resolution fail-loud position is explicitly flagged in the design itself as contestable and I did not find grounds to contest it: this host (Windows/Git Bash) already runs scripts/test_parallel.sh successfully all session (`which bash` -> /usr/bin/bash, confirmed again this gate), and CI's ubuntu-latest always has bash -- the fail-loud path is for an unobserved host shape, and failing loud there is the safer default per core-directives' 'never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures' posture (a silent fallback to serial mode would be exactly that kind of quiet behavior change).

Item 3 (failure-mode parity): §4.2's design (print full per-partition-log content on a Failed:/missing-Result: condition, before Mix.raise, re-using the same log-dir discovery from §1) is concretely specified enough to implement -- inputs/outputs and control flow are named, not hand-waved. It correctly notes CI's job log retention survives the mktemp dir's own discard, which is accurate (verified against .github/workflows/ci.yml -- no artifact-upload step exists today, and GitHub Actions does retain full step stdout regardless of runner-filesystem cleanup, consistent with core-directives' own 'gh run view --log-failed' guidance elsewhere in this repo).

Item 4 (wasm_hang / lua_wallclock_race stay serial): argued, not merely asserted -- section 2 cites the specific moduledoc mechanisms (wasmex's node-global native worker pool leak; ISS-0426's wall-clock contention, with ISS-0423's own discovered_side_effect record that 6-way parallelism is what surfaced that flake). No contrary evidence found; did not need to re-derive this experimentally since the design explicitly declines to touch scripts/test_parallel.sh or these two helpers at all, so there is no new mechanism to test.

Item 5 (ISS-0423 boundary): confirmed genuinely not absorbed -- section 5 correctly scopes ISS-0423 to test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's global `Sandbox.mode(:auto)` call defeating `async: true` WITHIN a partition/BEAM, which is orthogonal to this design's WHICH-subprocess-gets-shelled-out-to scope. Cross-checked against docs/issues/ISS-0423.yaml's own text indirectly via the design's quotes (matches what CODE-DESIGNER's own step-02 handoff summary states); no contradiction found.

Item 6 (no implementation code): confirmed by direct grep of the design file for ``` fences, `defmodule`, `  def `, `  defp ` -- zero matches. Section 6's function list is signatures/contracts only (names, input/output types in prose, explicit disclaimers like 'exact shape left to ELIXIR-DEV, this is a design-level contract not a literal type spec'). Matches the role file's Forbidden-section bar.

=== CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
git status --short: clean (probe file test/support/iss0428_probe_helper.ex created and removed; _build/test-partition-1, _build/test-partition-2, scratch/probe_stdout.log, and /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.* all removed). Re-ran `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --force` after cleanup: clean recompile, 209 files, no warnings, matching the pre-probe file count -- confirms no residual state. Did not modify the design document or lib/. Did not commit.

=== ROUTING ===
PASS with two findings for CODE-DESIGNER to address before ELIXIR-DEV implements (MAJOR finding 1 should be corrected -- reword §1.1's premise to be accurate; MINOR finding 2 should be clarified -- state the exit-code-vs-log-discovery check order explicitly). Neither finding is a BLOCKER: no vacuous-pass path exists in the design's actual specified algorithm, verified by direct experiment with a real injected ISS-0069-shaped warning. Per this gate's 'FAIL immediately on any single failed check' standard, judged against the checklist (AC coverage, no TBD, fully-specified signatures/error-shapes, cross-module deps listed, no implementation code) -- all pass. The two findings are quality/precision issues in an otherwise sound, verifiably-correct design, appropriately surfaced as findings rather than as gate failures, consistent with the role file's instruction to name specific gaps rather than rewrite the design myself.

issues.title: Design section 1.1's stated rationale for re-pointing the ISS-0069 check is factually imprecise: claims the wrapper's aggregate stdout never carries the target substring, but a compile-time warning from scripts/test_parallel.sh's own unredirected Step 1 (`mix compile`) does appear there -- verified by direct injection. Does not create a vacuous-pass hole (the design's actual algorithm only reads partition logs, proven to reliably catch the warning), but the premise as written should be corrected before ELIXIR-DEV builds from it.

Design section 1.2 does not state whether 'wrapper exit nonzero' (step 5) or 'partition-logs-in-<dir> line absent' (step 2) should be checked first when both are true simultaneously -- a real, verified case (mix compile failure inside test_parallel.sh exits before printing that line). Both orderings converge on a safe hard-failure, so this is an implementability/message-wording ambiguity, not a correctness gap.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a small rework addressing the two findings above (reword section 1.1's premise; clarify section 1.2's check ordering), then re-gate before ELIXIR-DEV implementation, per this gate's standard rework loop.
